title: Igris harness distribution manifest
description: Per-project declaration of agent prompt harnesses to mechanically regenerate from canonical sources. Core owns this schema; each project ships its own data manifest. See FR-136.

_schema.description: free-form human field-doc block; ignored by tooling

_harnesses_comment.description: free-form human doc for the `harnesses` map; ignored by tooling

version.description: Manifest format version. Bump only on a breaking schema change; FR-136 ships v1.

harnesses.description: TD-244 (BI-3): per-harness adapter descriptors for the SIXTH surface — the delegation mechanism / boot-injection. Maps a harness `type` to its `delegation_model`: `native-static` (the harness loads Igris agents statically → a skill delegates via `subagent_type:<agent>` directly, no recipe) or `dynamic-define` (the harness defines subagents at runtime → the per-session delegation recipe is appended to the harness's identity region by the compile identity pass, gated strictly on this value). A harness absent from this map defaults to `native-static` (back-compat: pre-TD-244 manifests project identity-only). Additive — still v1, no version bump. The identity compile/drift passes read `delegation_model` for each os_identity target's `type` to decide whether to append the recipe; absent/`native-static` → identity-only (existing golden fixtures unchanged).

delegation_model.description: native-static: statically-loaded Igris agents; the skill delegates abstractly and the adapter resolves to `subagent_type:<agent>`. dynamic-define: runtime subagent definition; the adapter region-merges the delegation recipe into the harness identity region at compile so the orchestrator is taught the read→define_subagent→invoke recipe once per session.

_contract.verification: re-derive via normalize_identity_shape + byte-compare the identity region (the identity drift branch in verify_identity); this is the BEHAVIORAL surface kind — no content is distributed, a per-harness behavior is injected at boot. Proves the 'two surface kinds' requirement against real code.

surfaces.description: FR-137: non-agent projection surfaces. 'skills' is fleshed out here (core-owned in surfaces-manifest.json, or personal via the FR-139 overlay). 'os_context' remains RESERVED for FR-140 (permissive). An absent or skills-only surfaces block validates. Additive flesh-out — no version bump (still v1). TD-191: `skills` is now an ARRAY of blocks (multi-source) — loaders normalize legacy single-object overlays to `[object]` on read so back-compat holds without a version bump. FR-161: `mcp_servers` is added as a 4th surface (ARRAY of blocks, mirroring `skills`); v1 is GLOBAL-ONLY (consumers treat every block as global even though the schema reuses $defs/scope for forward-compat). Additive — still v1, no version bump.

mcp_servers.description: FR-161: MCP-server projection blocks (FR-160 epic). An ARRAY of blocks, one per MCP server, mirroring `skills`. Each block declares the canonical command/args/env once; the compile pass (FR-164) merges it into each target harness's config. v1 GLOBAL-ONLY: `scope` is accepted for forward-compat but consumers treat every block as global. Core-owned blocks land in surfaces-manifest.json; personal blocks via the FR-139 overlay. NOTHING consumes this in FR-161 — schema/validators only.

os_identity.description: TD-233 (GAP-3 remediation): orchestrator-identity projection blocks — the 5th first-class surface. An ARRAY of blocks mirroring `mcp_servers`. Each block declares ONE canonical identity template (default <brain>/core/templates/identity.tmpl) projected into each target harness's natively auto-read project-root context file (gemini→GEMINI.md, codex→AGENTS.md; empirically confirmed 2026-06-10). Projection is a MERGE into an Igris-managed delimited region (markers), preserving pre-existing user content; drift checks ONLY the region. v1: declared by a project's own manifest (or core surfaces-manifest.json); personal-overlay blocks are accepted by the schema but NOT merged (no add-identity verb yet).

hooks.description: FR-180 (D7 — Option B): event-hook projection blocks — promoting hooks to a first-class surface so they ride the SAME flatten→compile→drift scaffold as skills/agents/mcp/identity. An ARRAY of blocks mirroring `mcp_servers`. Each block declares ONE event (SessionStart/SessionEnd/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PreCompact/PostCompact) + the canonical hook command (the shared script the harness runs) + per-harness `targets[{type, method:'merge'}]`. Projection is a config-MERGE into each harness's native hook surface (claude→.claude/settings.json hooks array, opencode→the FR-104 plugin events; codex→session_end only; gemini→N/A). Core-owned blocks land in surfaces-manifest.json; personal blocks via the FR-139 overlay — a personal block's command lives under ~/.igris/registry/hooks/ so the canonical re-merge (install/update/doctor) treats it as a DISTINCT-provenance Igris entry and PRESERVES it (the R2 refresh-overwrite hazard fix). v1 GLOBAL-ONLY: `scope` is accepted for forward-compat but consumers treat every block as global.

os_context.description: RESERVED for FR-140 (rules+prompts OS-context projection). Permissive until FR-140 fleshes it out; an absent block is the normal case in FR-137.

surface_contract.description: FR-202 (M0): the surface-plugin contract. DOC BLOCK ONLY — this $def is never $ref'd for validation; it formalizes the 3-concern lifecycle the core (compile_harnesses.sh + check_harness_drift.sh) owns for every wiring surface: declare -> distribute -> project -> verify. Each surface $def below (agent, skills_surface, mcp_surface, identity_surface, hook_surface) and the `harnesses` delegation descriptor carries a `_contract` object whose shape is described here. The contract GATES MEMBERSHIP: a thing is a wiring surface IFF it can fill all four fields — it has content DECLARED once (a canonical/source), DISTRIBUTED to the machine, PROJECTED into a per-harness native shape (a targets[] array), and VERIFIED by a drift verdict. A concept that cannot (no per-harness projection, no canonical declaration, or no drift-checkable artifact) is NOT a wiring surface — it belongs in core/os, a skill, or the brain. The schema enforces the membership gate structurally by requiring every surface block to carry `targets[]` (the projection points) and a `source`/`canonical` (the declaration). Adding a surface = a new `$defs/<x>_surface` + a registry entry in _common.sh (IGRIS_SURFACE_IDS) + project_<x>/verify_<x> plugins, with ZERO change to the two top scripts' dispatch loops. See README.md 'Surface-plugin contract' and MAINTAINING.md.

kind.description: material = content projected INTO a per-harness config/file (agents, skills, mcp, hooks). behavioral = a per-harness BEHAVIOR injected at boot rather than distributed content (delegation_model). The 'two surface kinds' requirement, proven against real code: agents/skills/mcp/hooks are material; the harnesses.delegation_model descriptor is the behavioral case.

distribution.description: How the surface's content reaches the machine. portable-format = a canonical .md/.toml the harness reads. native-add = a shared artifact already on disk merged in. npx = fetched/run via npx. n-a = no content distributed (behavioral surfaces — the behavior is injected, not shipped).

projection.description: How the declared content becomes a per-harness native shape. shape-emit = formats genuinely diverge so a translator emits each harness shape (agents: Claude MD / Gemini MD / OpenCode MD / Codex TOML). place-in-standard-dir = drop into a dir the harness reads natively. inject-at-boot = region-merge a recipe into the harness identity file (behavioral). merge-region = config-merge a delimited region/group into a native config (hooks, identity, mcp).

verification.description: The drift verdict the surface's verify_<x> plugin returns (MATCH / DRIFTED / MISSING). Names the existing verdict function/branch (e.g. agent-tree + symlink-realpath verdict; verify_hook_entry_present; verify_mcp_entry_drift secret-safe compare; verify_identity_file_drift region byte-compare).

scope.description: FR-155: scope-aware overlay. Absent → global (default, back-compat). `{type:'global'}` is also accepted; the compiler/drift treat both as 'emit unconditionally'. `{type:'project', paths:[...]}` emits ONLY when --project-root realpath ∈ realpath'd paths[]. CLI realpath's `--project` at WRITE time so paths[] entries are canonical; compile/drift realpath both PROJECT_ROOT and each entry at READ time (handles macOS /tmp ↔ /private/tmp).

skills_surface.description: FR-137/TD-191/FR-149/FR-151/FR-153/FR-155/FR-157/FR-171: ONE skills projection block. Multiple coexist as elements of `surfaces.skills[]`; each carries its OWN source/layer/targets so personal blocks compile ALONGSIDE the core block. For personal blocks `source` points at a registry-vendored path (L-516 universal copy-vendor). Valid (type, method) pairs: claude/symlink, codex/symlink, gemini/symlink, agents/symlink (registry-anchored per-skill symlinks), opencode/command (FR-171 thin command wrappers). The four symlink targets vendor identically — the per-harness compiler walks the registry-vendored skill tree. The `agents` target projects into the cross-CLI shared `~/.agents/skills/` standard that codex+gemini both read natively (FR-157). FR-171: `opencode/command` writes a thin `<command-dir>/<name>.md` wrapper whose body loads the canonical SKILL.md via OpenCode's `@file` directive (single source of truth stays the canonical SKILL.md). The legacy codex/compiler (AGENTS.md aggregator) + gemini/converter (per-skill TOML) pairs were retired by FR-153. `scope` (FR-155) is optional; absent → global. See L-519.

_contract.verification: per-skill tree-hash + per-target symlink-realpath / command-wrapper presence verdict (verify_skills)

source.description: Skills root dir holding {skill}/SKILL.md entries. A leading '~' or an absolute path is used verbatim; otherwise resolved vs --project-root. Default ~/.igris/core/skills.

layer.description: FR-139 provenance seam: 'core' (declared in surfaces-manifest.json) or 'personal' (contributed by the FR-139 overlay).

path.description: symlink (claude/codex/gemini/agents): output dir under which each <skill>/ becomes a symlink to its registry-vendored canonical (FR-149/FR-151/FR-153). command (opencode, FR-171): the OpenCode command dir under which each <name>.md thin wrapper is written. The legacy compiler/converter methods were retired by FR-153.

mcp_surface.description: FR-161 (FR-160 epic): ONE MCP-server projection block. Multiple coexist as elements of `surfaces.mcp_servers[]`. `canonical` declares the command/args/env ONCE (env values are ${VAR} references, never inline secrets); the FR-164 compile pass merges this into each target harness config (config-MERGE, not symlink). `targets` carries a SEPARATE enum from agents/skills — MCP adds a 4th harness (`opencode`) and its `method` is always the const `merge`. v1 is GLOBAL-ONLY: `scope` is accepted (reuses $defs/scope for forward-compat) but consumers treat every block as global. `startup_timeout_sec` is a Codex-only passthrough. See FR-160 plan §FR-160a.

_contract.verification: secret-safe per-(mcp,target) entry compare via verify_mcp_entry_drift (MATCH/DRIFTED/MISSING; codex literals re-resolved inside the compare, never printed)

layer.description: FR-139 provenance seam: 'core' (declared in surfaces-manifest.json) or 'personal' (contributed by the FR-139 overlay).

env.description: values are ${VAR} references, NOT inline secrets (enforced at write-time by the FR-162 verb)

identity_surface.description: TD-233: ONE orchestrator-identity projection block. `source` is the canonical identity template (tokens {{IGRIS_VERSION}} + {{HARNESS_SELF_NAME}}; Model A — 'the agent IS Igris AI'; Model B is parked). `version_source` optionally names a JSON file whose top-level `version` key resolves {{IGRIS_VERSION}} (the igris-ai repo points it at cli/package.json so compile/drift/CI all re-derive from the checkout); absent → <brain>/config.json. `targets[].filename` is the harness's natively auto-read identity file, resolved per the FR-154 3-case shape (`~/` → $HOME, absolute → verbatim, else → --project-root). `method` is always the const `file` (atomic region-merge file write). `scope` reuses $defs/scope (FR-155).

_contract.verification: verify_identity_file_drift — re-derive the expected delimited region via the shared normalize_identity_shape and byte-compare ONLY the Igris-managed region (MATCH/DRIFTED). NOTE: the harnesses.delegation_model descriptor (see its _contract) is the BEHAVIORAL surface kind that rides this same identity pass via inject-at-boot.

source.description: Canonical identity template path (3-case resolution). Default: <brain>/core/templates/identity.tmpl.

version_source.description: JSON file (3-case resolution) whose top-level `version` resolves {{IGRIS_VERSION}}. Default: <brain>/config.json. Declare a repo-committed file (e.g. cli/package.json) when the projected files are committed-as-canonical, so CI and every contributor re-derive identical bytes.

layer.description: FR-139 provenance seam: 'core' (declared in a base manifest) or 'personal' (overlay). FR-180 (D6) lifted the v1 'overlay accepted but NOT merged' restriction — personal os_identity blocks now merge base++overlay (in merge_overlay_manifest) and project like core; a personal (type, filename) target that collides with a core one is a hard error.

filename.description: The harness's natively auto-read identity file (GEMINI.md / AGENTS.md), resolved per the 3-case shape — project-root-relative in the confirmed v1 map.

hook_surface.description: FR-180 (D7 - Option B): ONE event-hook projection block. Multiple coexist as elements of `surfaces.hooks[]`. `event` is the canonical Igris event name; `canonical.command` is the shared hook script the harness runs (a personal block's command lives under ~/.igris/registry/hooks/<name>/ - a distinct provenance prefix the canonical re-merge preserves, fixing the R2 refresh-overwrite hazard; a core block's lives under $HOME/.igris/core/hooks/shared/). Optional `canonical.matcher` (tool-glob for PreToolUse/PostToolUse) + `canonical.timeout` (seconds). `targets` carries a SEPARATE enum - claude (settings.json hooks array), opencode (the FR-104 plugin), and antigravity (FR-181: config-merge into ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json, gemini-cli hook format, via the antigravity bridge); codex supports only session_end and gemini-cli 0.45.0 has a `gemini hooks` subcommand (full onboarding tracked under FR-182, so gemini is documented, not yet projected). `method` is always the const `merge`. v1 is GLOBAL-ONLY: `scope` is accepted (reuses $defs/scope for forward-compat) but consumers treat every block as global.

_contract.verification: verify_hook_entry_present — presence-based MATCH/MISSING (the hook is identified by its command path, not a full byte-shape; opencode asserts the FR-104 plugin exists)

event.description: The Igris portable event this hook fires on (the same six PORTABLE_EVENTS the canonical-settings.json hooks block declares).

layer.description: FR-139 provenance seam: 'core' (declared in surfaces-manifest.json) or 'personal' (contributed by the FR-139 overlay). A 'personal' block's command lives under ~/.igris/registry/hooks/ so the canonical re-merge preserves it (R2).

command.description: The hook command the harness runs (a shell script path). Personal blocks: ~/.igris/registry/hooks/<name>/<event>.sh; core blocks: $HOME/.igris/core/hooks/shared/<event>.sh.

matcher.description: Tool-name glob (PreToolUse/PostToolUse only), e.g. 'Write|Edit'. Omitted - fires for all tools / non-tool events.

timeout.description: Per-hook timeout in seconds (optional; passthrough to the harness hook entry).

_contract.verification: per-agent tree-hash + per-target symlink/hardlink-realpath verdict (verify_agents); formats genuinely diverge (Claude MD / Gemini MD / OpenCode MD / Codex TOML) so compile_md_agent_target translates each per-harness shape

layer.description: RESERVED / forward-compat for FR-139 (Layer-2 customization registry). Provenance only - the compiler enforces the Core/Personal boundary physically via separate base + overlay manifest files (see FR-136 plan section 2), NOT via this field. Defaults to 'core' when absent. FR-139 may write 'personal' (or a namespaced value) on overlay entries.

dir.description: canonical prompt dir, resolved relative to --project-root

body_exception.description: optional; basename of a body-exceptions/<name>.json sidecar

path.description: output harness path. Resolved per 3-case shape (FR-154): leading `~/` expands against $HOME, `/abs/...` is verbatim, otherwise relative to --project-root. FR-171: `opencode` agent targets project a registry-anchored symlink (OpenCode's agent loader follows symlinks) to harness.opencode.md.
